decisions.reason: Moving the SK6812 LEDs to the switchable 5V rail necessarily removes them from DCDC1's documented 3.3V load coverage.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Doesn't the 5V_EN pin solve this? We can cut the entire 5V rail via GPIO3 when LEDs are not needed, dropping standby current to zero.

decisions.reason: The client places the LEDs on the switchable 5V rail, replacing the daughterboard's previously recorded 3.3V supply.

source_message.speaker: client

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already records the LEDs as 5V-rail loads and the GPIO3-controlled standby policy.
The existing same-message MODIFY already changes the LED supply to 5V and records the 5V_EN standby-power control.
The 5V LED-rail decision does not change USB data routing, enumeration, flashing, or connector sourceability.
Switching the LEDs through the downstream 5V rail does not change the AXP2101's role as the normal-operation system power source.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records the operational function of the interboard 5V_EN signal.
The LED power-rail decision does not alter I2C pull-ups, conditioning, speed, cable constraints, or routing.
The source uses the already established GPIO3 control and does not revise the general GPIO-assignment policy.
The 5V_EN control decision does not change the selected ESP32-S3 controller family.
The source concerns LED standby power and does not change the sensor board's connector-fanout role.
The source does not change BOM completion, component sourcing, population, or design-justification requirements.
